source.name: Fintraffic Digitraffic Railway
source.attribution: Traffic data source Fintraffic / digitraffic.fi, licence CC BY 4.0
source.note: Public operational feed. This analysis does not speak for Fintraffic or any operator.

method.excluded: Cargo, shunting, locomotive, on-track machines, test drives
method.padding: median scheduled leg run time minus 5th percentile of observed run times
method.line: modal route signature (operated stop sequence), expresses absorbed as subsequences

counterfactual.method: Redistribute the line's total padding across legs in proportion to measured delay survival, conserving total scheduled run time, then replay observed delay deltas through the new schedule.
counterfactual.assumes: Each train's running behaviour is unchanged. Taking slack off a leg cannot make that leg generate delay in this arithmetic, though it would in the world.

mechanism.claim: Delay survival across a leg falls as that leg's recovery margin rises.
mechanism.note: The trend is strong but not monotonic bucket to bucket; read the correlation and the end points, not each step.

limitations: Cause attribution covers ~1% of rows: we can say a delay survived a leg, mostly not why.
The technical minimum run time is a 5th-percentile proxy, not an engineering figure.
Samples thin beyond about four stops.
Lines separate when their recovery margin differs and not otherwise; the picker must not rank lines by quality.
Margin predicting survival is an association measured across legs, not a controlled experiment.
Finland only. No capacity, rolling-stock, crew or cost model.
The counterfactual is arithmetic on observed delays, not an operational plan.
